preamble: A velar stop becomes the velar nasal [ŋ] next to a nasal. In Korean and in Sanskrit sandhi a stop assimilates to a following nasal consonant. In Indonesian and Malay the nasal prefix meN- fuses with a root-initial k, which is replaced by [ŋ] (nasal substitution). Welsh nasal mutation, which also comes from an earlier nasal, gives a voiceless velar nasal [ŋ̊] rather than [ŋ].

examples.note: Coda /k/ becomes [ŋ] before a nasal onset
meN- + k: the k is replaced by [ŋ]
External sandhi: a final stop assimilates to the nasal of the same place before a nasal

sources: Sohn, H.-M. (1999). The Korean Language. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521361231
Whitney, W. D. (1889). Sanskrit Grammar (2nd ed.). Harvard University Press. Wikisource. https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Sanskrit_Grammar_(Whitney)
